collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A child asks why people die, and two adults give very different answers: let both answers stand, or pick one.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s pet gecko died this morning, and (subject.he/she) wants to know why things have to die. (friend) says that everything that lives must one day rest, and its body goes back to feed the island. (third) says the gecko's spirit has gone on somewhere it will be happy. (subject) looks from one to the other. What should they tell (subject.him/her)?

text_only.reason: a death only talked about (or the word's everyday sense); nobody dies -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) and (third) look at each other and agree that nobody knows for certain, and that (subject) can believe whichever feels right, or both, or neither. (subject) thinks about this, then asks if the gecko can be buried under the flowers. They bury it together.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) and (third) start arguing about which answer is right, quite gently, and then less gently. (subject) wanders off in the middle and buries the gecko on (subject.his/her) own, under the flowers, and sings it a little song. When the adults find (subject.him/her), they stop arguing.
